newsitem.title: GERMANY: Genscher slams EMU delay talk and "criteria trap".
newsitem.headline: Genscher slams EMU delay talk and "criteria trap".

text.p: Former German foreign minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher warned on Friday that delaying Europe's single currency would lead Bonn into "ice-cold isolation" and urged flexibility on the euro's criteria to launch it on time.
Genscher, still an influential voice on foreign affairs and within his Free Democratic Party (FDP), also warned the powerful Bundesbank against being used by anti-European forces.

His statement, in an article for the Nordsee-Zeitung daily, was the latest in a widening public debate in Germany over how to launch Europe's monetary union (EMU) now that Bonn looks unable to meet the criteria precisely.

"Supporters of a delay just won't give up ... (but) they are playing a dangerous game," Genscher wrote, saying Bonn had to meet the 1999 launch date and fulfil the Maastricht criteria with a deficit only three percent of gross domestic product.

"Whoever claims the treaty demands a pinpoint landing on a 3.0 percent target is giving Maastricht a different meaning that its text," he wrote. "He is building a criteria trap in which he can easily get caught."

Genscher, Bonn's top diplomat from 1974 to 1992, also said German politicians should not use events in other European states as a pretext to argue for a delay, as press reports say leaders of Finance Minister Theo Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU) are considering.
"The change in government in Paris doesn't apply here," he wrote. "The new govenrment's programme is not yet fixed.

"But Jacques Delors vouches for the European course of the new French government. The prime minister, the foreign minister, ministers (Martine) Aubry and (Elisabeth) Guigou -- and not only them -- are all proven Europeans."
